items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The names say what they do (validateWindowName, buildWindowClause, NamedWindowDefinition), and the .window() methods follow the formatting of the surrounding builder methods. The tests are well organised by describe blocks.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The shared buildWindowClause is reused by all five dialects. However, the same ~20-line .window() body, including the SelectionProxyHandler logic, is copied into all five builders. The diff also contains an unrelated `.mapWith(query.decoder)` edit in the pg, mysql and singlestore dialects.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Window names, ntile and nthValue arguments, preceding()/following() arguments and frame ordering are all validated. Tests cover NaN, Infinity, negatives and non-integers, and check that from must not come after to. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The windows field is optional and .window() is added to all five dialects. But the agent also changed existing behaviour: `).mapWith(query.decoder)` was added to the selection-field handling in pg, mysql and singlestore dialect.ts. That changes result decoding for existing queries that don't use windows.
